title: Azure OpenAI in Business Central AL: Managed vs Unmanaged
summary: The post compares two ways for AL code to authenticate to Azure OpenAI in Business Central. SetAuthorization uses your own Azure OpenAI deployment, which gives you control but you pay for and maintain it. SetManagedResourceAuthorization uses the Microsoft-managed resource, which is included in the Business Central allotment, and it gets grounded Bing search when Copilot web search is enabled.
key_points: With SetAuthorization you use your own Azure OpenAI deployment and control the model, update timing, region and tuning, but costs go to your Azure subscription
SetManagedResourceAuthorization still needs an account name and API key, but its usage counts against the Business Central allotment and Microsoft maintains the service
If Copilot web search is enabled, the managed resource also gets grounded Bing search, so responses can include current web data
Grounded search is a preview feature and adds another layer to the OpenAI traffic, so it does not suit cases where data containment matters
The managed resource moves to newer models as old ones are deprecated, and prompts may then need retesting

quotes.text: The Managed Resource is part of your Business Central allotment and is not billed to your Azure Subscription.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the key cost advantage of using managed resources over unmanaged Azure OpenAI

quotes.text: What Grounded Bing Search does is provide the ability for the OpenAI Agent to utilize a search engine to supplement its response.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies the primary benefit that makes managed resource attractive for real-time information needs

quotes.text: What works for prompting in one model may not work correctly in a newer model.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights a critical consideration for managed resources when Microsoft upgrades the underlying model
